chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said:

I asked him about the throwing of the Jamarat on the Day of Nahr (Eid al-Adha). Why is it thrown alone, and no other Jamarat are thrown on the Day of Nahr? He said: 'They used to throw all of them, but they left that practice.'
I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, should I throw them all?' He said, 'Do not throw them. Do you not desire to do as I do?'

He said: I said to him, 'When a man completes his Hajj and there is something upon him, requiring a blood sacrifice (dam) for it, is it sufficient for him to slaughter it when he returns to his family?' He said, 'Yes.' And he said, 'As far as I know, he should give it in charity.'

key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood sacrifice (dam) required for Hajj faults
key_terms.رَمْيِ الْجِمَارِ: Throwing of the Jamarat (pillars) during Hajj
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Nahr (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah, Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on throwing the Jamarat on Eid al-Adha and where should the Hajj sacrifice be slaughtered if incurred after leaving Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the principle of *ittiba'* (following the Imam) in ritual variations, specifically regarding the reduction of Jamarat throws on the Day of Nahr from the historical norm. It further clarifies the flexibility of expiation (*dam*) for unintentional violations, permitting the sacrifice to be performed in the pilgrim's hometown with the meat distributed as charity, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams.
